# Jordan Loewen-Colón

> Indigenous Taíno technologist and Responsible AI strategist — advisory, consulting, workshops, and keynotes on AI ethics, Indigenous data sovereignty, and the politics of emerging technology.

Jordan Loewen-Colón works at the intersection of artificial intelligence, culture, new media, and data justice. He is a professor at Queen's University's Smith School of Business and Department of Computing, a former Tech Policy Fellow at the Aspen Institute, and has co-authored research published in Harvard Business Review and Springer's AI & Society. He is cofounder and former CEO of Supernova Immersives, an AI-augmented VR mental health company ($1M+ valuation, Founder Institute). His forthcoming book is Reality Technologies.

He defends the Right to Opacity — that people, cultures, and knowledge systems should not be rendered fully transparent, extractable, or machine-readable simply because technology makes it possible. His concept of Empire 2.0 describes the digital extraction of Indigenous languages, biometric data, and cultural knowledge under the language of innovation and open data.

## Available for

- Quarterly advisory retainer
- Consulting projects (4–12 weeks, scoped)
- Workshops (half-day to two-day) for product, policy, and leadership teams
- Keynotes (30–60 min): "Doing AI Differently", "Empire 2.0", "Many Models One World", "Human–AI Ensembles", "Artificial Opportunity"
- Honoraria adjusted for universities, public-interest organizations, and Indigenous-led work
